prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1125; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss was received for a side impact at an intersection, with the claimant reporting neck and back strain. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show damage that lines up with the described impact, and the vehicle damage is consistent with a side collision. The file has no independent witness statements, so the photos carry most of the weight at this stage.

Entry 3: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the crash. The responding officer's notes match the basic sequence of events given at intake.

Entry 4: The claimant's account of the collision has stayed the same in every conversation so far, including the initial call and the recorded statement. No change in the description of how the crash happened has been noted.

Entry 5: Records search shows no earlier damage to the vehicle on file, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The driver is a member of the policyholder's household and is covered as such.

Entry 6: Medical records were requested through counsel. No prior injury to the neck or back has been identified in the claimant's history, and the reported strain is a plausible result of a crash of this type.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course of care, with the claimant attending scheduled visits and progressing steadily. The treating provider's notes show symptoms easing over the period of care.

Entry 8: Treatment has tapered as the claimant improved, and the most recent records show fewer visits and reduced reported pain. Current status is being monitored against the medical file.

Entry 9: File reviewed. Vehicle damage, police confirmation of the claimant's presence, consistent accounts, and medical course all align with the reported loss, and the claim remains open pending final medical documentation from counsel.
